prompt: Which is NOT a measure of center?
hint: A measure of center gives one typical value. A measure of spread tells how far apart the values are.

hints.text: A measure of center gives one typical value. A measure of spread tells how far apart the values are.
Mean, median and mode each name a typical value in the data. One choice is found by subtracting the smallest value from the largest, which describes something different.
The range (choice C) is not a measure of center, because it measures spread.

explanation: Measures of center describe a typical or middle value of a data set.
The mean, the median and the mode each do this in a different way, so A, B and D are measures of center.
The range is the largest value minus the smallest, which tells how spread out the data is.
So the range, choice C, is not a measure of center.
